title: Excepciones, debugging y logging seguro
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only concepts marked USABLE in the effective prior ledger count as learned.

roadmap_expectation.T1: specific exception types, raise, chaining, recovery boundaries and cleanup
roadmap_expectation.T2: traceback/debugger, minimal reproduction, falsifiable hypotheses and root cause
roadmap_expectation.T3: logging levels/structure, correlation IDs and PII redaction
roadmap_expectation.T4: fail-fast versus quarantine, idempotency and transient-only retries
roadmap_expectation.gate: auditable log that never records complete email/phone/address and distinguishes data, config and provider failures

later_boundaries.S10: modules, packaging, CLI and process exit codes

live_site.note: Public fetch returned DisabledError; no hydrated-render parity claim is made.

audit_metadata.audience_assumption: ZERO_TECH capable learner with only effective prior USABLE concepts

reference_checks.source: Learning programming from erroneous worked-examples, Learning and Instruction 2021
Debug It: A debugging practicing system, Computers & Education 1999

adversarial_review.most_likely_beginner_failure: The learner thinks that catching a fatal exception, printing 'fatal' or 'abort', and continuing to normal process termination is fail-fast; the canonical S09 demos repeat the S08 exit-status misconception and actually return process status 0.
adversarial_review.suspected_hidden_prerequisite: Custom exception classes require class/inheritance syntax before S11; module imports, context managers and higher-order callback functions are also used without being safely creditable.
adversarial_review.most_likely_misconception: That masking the explicit log message guarantees log.exception/traceback output contains no PII, even when the exception message itself contains raw sensitive data.

confirmed_findings.evidence: CP-N1-C, CASO-LIM-009 and 'pipeline de familiaridad' appear as internal project/domain labels without one stable learner-facing introduction.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No internal curriculum-code vocabulary.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner sees operational goals framed through unexplained internal identifiers.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: They cannot tell whether CP-N1-C is a project increment, test gate, package, file or operational environment, and 'familiaridad' has no defined domain meaning.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Expand CP-N1-C once as the third Level-1 project increment; define CASO-LIM-009 as the synthetic incident case; replace or define 'pipeline de familiaridad'.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The text says 'el tipo de error ya es un diagnóstico' and that a custom exception name answers data/config/provider before reading the trace.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: First formal exception model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Exception type is evidence, not a complete diagnosis. KeyError, ValueError or OSError can arise in multiple layers; even custom types are only as accurate as the code that classified them.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner stops investigation after seeing an exception class and treats classification as root cause.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say the exception type narrows the search and should encode the layer/policy when the program can justify that classification; traceback and context are still required.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The opening says read a trace bottom-up; T2-A says frames are 'del más reciente al más profundo (o viceversa según la herramienta)'. The standard Python traceback prints the call chain and ends with the innermost failing frame followed by exception type/value.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: This section is responsible for the first usable traceback-reading model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Two incompatible direction models are given for the same artifact.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot distinguish caller frames from the frame where the exception arose and may start debugging the wrong layer.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach one concrete standard-Python trace: top frame = earlier caller, later frames = deeper calls, last frame = immediate failure location, final line = exception class/message; mention alternative tool presentations only after that model is stable.

confirmed_findings.evidence: class ValidationError(Exception) and class ParseError(Exception) introduce class definition and inheritance, while the V3 roadmap first teaches classes/instances in S11.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No usable class/inheritance model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The first formal exception lesson hides raise/chaining behind future OOP syntax.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can copy a custom exception declaration without understanding class, base class, inheritance or why Exception appears in parentheses.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach raise/chaining first with built-in exceptions. If custom exceptions are indispensable, add a bounded microdefinition that this one-line class creates a named exception subtype, then defer general class semantics to S11.

confirmed_findings.evidence: str(raw).strip().replace(',', '.') silently interprets every comma as a decimal separator before Decimal parsing.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S08 established that source formats require explicit contracts and raw preservation.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A value such as '1,234' can mean one-thousand-two-hundred-thirty-four under one contract or one-point-two-three-four under another; the function chooses silently.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner mistakes successful parsing for correct interpretation and may corrupt amounts while focusing on exception mechanics.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Declare the accepted monetary text format before parsing and reject ambiguous separators rather than globally replacing commas.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The alt text places a boundary between parse and validate 'after which the row can no longer be sent to quarantine'; the caption says after deciding only a summary remains. In the lesson's own policy, validation is precisely where a bad row can be classified and quarantined.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: T1-B should establish where recovery decisions belong.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The diagram assigns a false point-of-no-return to row recovery.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may believe a row that reaches validation is too late to quarantine, contradicting T4-A and the S08 pipeline.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Redraw the boundary around the batch/publication edge: parse/validate can still classify a row; after publishing/committing the batch, recovery semantics change. Make the diagram match the stated data-vs-config policy.

confirmed_findings.evidence: S08 left with/context managers unmastered. S09 says 'with hace lo mismo ... vía context managers' without defining context manager or the important difference that __exit__ may perform behavior beyond simple cleanup.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: with was MENTION_ONLY at S09 entry.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A still-weak concept is reused as if mastered and is explained by another widow term.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner treats with as syntactic sugar identical to finally without understanding resource acquisition/exit behavior.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Microdefine: a context manager controls setup/cleanup around a with block; for file-like objects it guarantees close on exit. Do not equate all context managers with finally.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Both examples label configuration errors fatal/abort but catch RuntimeError at the outer demo boundary and merely print it. Executed as standalone Python processes, both terminated with return code 0.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S01 introduced exit codes, but S08 left process-exit semantics MISCONCEPTION_RISK; S09 explicitly promises fail-fast.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The lesson repeats print-theater: an error label is shown while the operating system sees normal success.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner believes 'fatal:' or 'abort:' on stdout/stderr is equivalent to a failing job status, so schedulers/CI can treat failed jobs as success.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: For the fatal demonstration, let the exception escape the process or re-raise after logging. Explicit exit-code mapping belongs at the S10 CLI boundary, but S09 must not claim a caught-and-swallowed demo is fail-fast.
confirmed_findings.execution_evidence: Canonical boundaries.py and failfast_quarantine.py logic both returned process code 0 after printing fatal/abort.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Caption: 'Atrapar Exception en el origen borra el tipo; atraparlo todo en la frontera pierde el contexto de dónde ocurrió.' Earlier prose correctly says except Exception does not itself erase traceback. Re-raising preserves the concrete exception type; a boundary logger using traceback/log.exception can preserve origin frames.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: First debugging boundary model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The visual teaches two false causal rules and contradicts T1-A.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner avoids all broad boundary catches for the wrong reason or believes merely entering except Exception converts a ValueError/KeyError into generic Exception.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Caption should say broad catches can mix policies; swallowing/replacing without chaining loses evidence. Catching at a process boundary can be appropriate when the original exception/traceback is preserved and the error is re-raised or mapped deliberately.

confirmed_findings.evidence: T1-A encourages including the problematic raw value in exception messages. T2-A proposes traceback.format_exc; T3-B says mask the explicit log message then use log.exception. Python log.exception attaches exception information/traceback, including the exception message. Execution confirmed a full email in ValueError reappeared below a masked logging message.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S09 gate promises logs without complete email/phone/address.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The redaction policy sanitizes one message channel but not exception text carried by traceback/log.exception.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner logs 'email=a***@...' and assumes the event is safe while the traceback contains 'ValueError: email completo: ana.rojas@...'.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Prohibit sensitive raw values in exception messages that may be logged; store safe identifiers/reason codes, and ensure any full diagnostic data remains in separately protected evidence. Teach that log.exception includes the exception message as well as stack frames.
confirmed_findings.execution_evidence: log.exception('email=%s','a***@...') following ValueError('email completo: ana.rojas@...') emitted the full email in the traceback.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The outcome promises traceback and debugger. The paragraph names breakpoint()/pdb, but the only code example filters traceback.format_exc; no debugger command, breakpoint state inspection or continue/step behavior is demonstrated.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Debugger is new.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner is told the tool exists but receives no usable interaction model.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: They cannot use breakpoint()/pdb from theory alone and may confuse traceback formatting with interactive debugging.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Either narrow the outcome to traceback diagnosis or add a minimal, explicitly local-only debugger walkthrough: enter breakpoint, inspect one safe variable, continue. Keep PII warning.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The learning outcome promises minimal repro with hypotheses and regression tests. Theory demonstrates a shortest failing string and discusses red→green, but shows no falsifiable hypothesis execution, no failing assertion/test, no code repair and no green rerun.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Simple checks are allowed before systematic pytest later.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Essential debugging workflow is externalized to later practice despite being a core S09 outcome.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner equates reproducing the exception with finding/fixing root cause and has no model for converting the repro into a guard against recurrence.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one explicit cycle: hypothesis -> small assertion that fails -> minimal code fix -> same assertion passes -> nearby negative case remains correct.

confirmed_findings.evidence: 'Minimal repro' is operationalized as min((n for n,_ in bad), key=len), which finds the shortest failing value among already-observed exceptions; it is not necessarily the smallest reproducible program/environment. The expression also uses a generator expression and key= compactly despite those constructs not being safely mastered.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: for is usable; generator expressions are not.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The concept is narrowed to string length and hidden behind irrelevant compact syntax.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner thinks minimal reproduction means shortest input only, and may fail to isolate setup/state/code dependencies.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Define minimal repro as the smallest self-contained setup that still produces the behavior. Choose the example manually here and use explicit loops if reduction itself is not the lesson target.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson promises structured fields but code embeds stage=..., record_id=..., duration_ms=... inside a free-form message string. No LogRecord fields or JSON object are created.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S09 is responsible for the first logging structure model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Parseable text by convention is presented as if fields are first-class structured data.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner expects aggregators to filter stage/correlation_id reliably without a parser or explicit structured formatter and may silently break dashboards by changing message wording.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use extra={...} to add stable LogRecord fields and a formatter that emits them, or label key=value messages 'semi-structured text' and explain the parser contract.

confirmed_findings.evidence: decimal, io, traceback, logging and time are imported, while the roadmap teaches modules/imports in S10 and prior import mechanics remain MENTION_ONLY.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No full module model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Necessary stdlib names remain incantations.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot explain why some names require import, what from X import Y means, or why logging.getLogger belongs to a module namespace.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Reuse a bounded one-sentence bridge: these are modules included with Python; import makes their names available here. Defer namespaces/package mechanics to S10.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Outcome promises propagating correlation_id and masking email, phone and address. Theory code creates one local corr variable and sends it to one log call; it never passes the ID across CLI/service/repo-like layers. mask_email and mask_phone exist, but mask_address does not.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Functions remain only partially consolidated, so propagation must be shown simply and explicitly.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Two named pieces of the outcome are prose-only.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can print a correlation ID once but does not know how the same identifier reaches nested operations; they also have no address-redaction example despite the privacy gate.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Show two small functions receiving/passing correlation_id explicitly and add a deliberately coarse address masker or narrow the outcome to fields actually taught.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The text says a***@ejemplo.pe 'no expone a la persona' and that a log shareable after masking is safe for team debugging. Masking reduces exposure but does not guarantee anonymity; initial, domain, record_id, correlation_id, timestamps and surrounding events can still identify a person or case.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Privacy reasoning should avoid absolute guarantees.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A mitigation is framed as elimination of privacy risk.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may broaden log access because fields are masked even though the combined event remains linkable/sensitive.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say masking reduces exposure; logs still require access controls, retention rules and data-minimization. Do not call masked records anonymous.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Provider examples include 'timeout S3', 'HTTP 503', env ROOT_PATH, service/repo and provider semantics before HTTP/API material is taught in S12 and config/CLI in S10. 'S3' is especially ambiguous with course Section 3 versus AWS S3.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No HTTP status or S3/provider contract model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Retry taxonomy is explained through unexplained future infrastructure jargon.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot tell whether S3 is Amazon S3, Section 3 or another service, and may memorize 503 as retryable without understanding an HTTP response.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use Python-level examples first: TimeoutError for a simulated external call. Add HTTP 503/S3 only as labeled future examples after a microdefinition or defer them to S12.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The text says 'Éxito parcial es válido si el manifest cuadra' and 'Cuarentena + conteos > crash total'.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S08 reconciliation is accounting evidence, not a complete business acceptance policy.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Arithmetic reconciliation is treated as sufficient for partial success even if all rows are quarantined, a critical source is missing, or a policy sets a maximum reject rate.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner publishes a technically reconciled but operationally unusable batch.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: State reconciliation is necessary, not sufficient. Partial success also requires the source-specific policy to allow the observed quarantine classes/rate and all critical inputs to be present.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson says operations are idempotent when they use the same write key and suggests (source, record_id, version)+payload hash. A key alone does not prevent duplicate side effects; the receiving persistence/action must enforce uniqueness, overwrite/upsert semantics, or remember processed keys.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: First explicit idempotency/retry model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Identity of an operation is confused with enforcement of idempotent behavior.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner adds an idempotency key to a normal INSERT but still performs two inserts on retry and believes the system is safe.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Define idempotency behavior first: repeating the same logical request has the same externally observable result. Then explain an idempotency key is one mechanism only when the receiver actually uses it to detect/reuse a prior result or perform an upsert.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The code retries an arbitrary callback fn and demonstrates only a counter; it neither performs nor protects a side effect. It therefore cannot demonstrate the idempotency requirement named in the outcome. The example also depends on passing functions as values, a concept not safely mastered from S05.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: for/try may be taught here; higher-order callback design is not a necessary prerequisite.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The safety condition for retries exists only in prose, while executable code teaches retrying any callable that raises TimeoutError.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner copies fetch_with_retry around state-changing operations without a deduplication/upsert contract.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: First demonstrate retry around a side-effect-free read, explicitly saying why it is safe. Then show a tiny fake store that rejects/reuses an already-seen idempotency key before claiming safe retry of writes.

confirmed_findings.evidence: TimeoutError, HTTP 503 and 'red' are presented as transient categories, but retry safety depends on operation/provider semantics and a timeout may occur after a remote side effect. The no-retry demo uses lambda plus (_ for _ in ()).throw(...), adding future syntax unrelated to retry reasoning.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No HTTP/provider protocol model; lambda/generator expressions are not usable.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Retry eligibility is reduced to an exception/status label and the clearest negative case is obscured by code-golf syntax.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner retries every timeout automatically or cannot explain how the ValueError demo raises at all.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say 'candidate transient errors defined by the provider contract' and require idempotent/known-outcome semantics. Replace the lambda/generator trick with def bad_data(_): raise ValueError('dato malo').

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: El trabajo ingest_clientes falló a las 02:10... KeyError: 'monto'... correo completo...
issues: good incident motivation but no causal bridge from KeyError to classification
paragraph_audit.improved_content: A las 02:10 falla el job sintético de ingesta de clientes. La persona de guardia ve un traceback que termina en KeyError: 'monto'. Ese dato todavía no demuestra si la causa es una fila sin esa clave, una configuración incorrecta o un bug en el código que eligió el diccionario equivocado. Además, el mensaje contiene un correo completo. S09 aprenderá a conservar la evidencia técnica necesaria sin convertir el log en otra fuga de datos.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: el tipo de error ya es un diagnóstico... el nombre del error contesta la pregunta...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: El tipo de excepción es una primera pista, no el diagnóstico completo. ValueError, KeyError u OSError acotan qué clase de operación falló; una excepción de dominio puede además expresar la política de tu pipeline. Aun así, debes revisar el contexto y el traceback para confirmar dónde y por qué se produjo.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Una traza se lee de abajo hacia arriba... abajo el qué falló y arriba cómo llegaste.
paragraph_audit.improved_content: En el traceback estándar de Python, los frames aparecen desde llamadas exteriores hacia llamadas cada vez más profundas. El último frame es normalmente la línea de código donde se produjo la excepción; después aparece la clase y el mensaje del error. Empieza por ese último frame de tu código y sube por los callers cuando necesites entender cómo llegó hasta allí.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: correlation_id... a***@ejemplo.pe basta para reconocer un caso y no expone a la persona...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un correlation_id aleatorio acompaña los eventos de una misma corrida para poder reunirlos después. Antes de registrar datos del caso, minimiza y enmascara los campos personales. Una máscara como a***@ejemplo.pe reduce exposición, pero no vuelve anónimo al evento: el log sigue necesitando controles de acceso, retención limitada y solo los campos estrictamente necesarios.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: config mal -> falla de inmediato; fila mal -> aparta y continúa
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Clasifica el fallo según el alcance que compromete. Una configuración necesaria para todo el lote normalmente obliga a abortar; una fila individual inválida puede ir a cuarentena si el contrato permite continuar. La decisión debe estar escrita por fuente: una tasa de cuarentena excesiva o la ausencia de un input crítico también puede hacer fallar un lote reconciliado.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: ¿qué puede hacer con esto alguien que no escribió el código...? conteos reconciliados de S08...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: La pregunta guía es operativa: ¿qué evidencia necesita una persona que no escribió el código para decidir el siguiente paso? Cada rechazo debe indicar una clase de fallo, un correlation_id y una referencia segura a la evidencia. S08 introdujo la reconciliación de conteos; en S09 no la daremos por correcta hasta que el flujo de error preserve también el estado de fallo del proceso.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Bloque de referencia...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Bloque de referencia: resume el orden de los subtemas, el criterio de cierre y los límites de S09.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: T1 excepciones... T2 diagnóstico... T3 registro... T4 resiliencia...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: T1 construye el flujo de una excepción: raise, propagación, captura, else/finally y chaining. T2 enseña a leer el traceback y reducir un fallo a un caso reproducible con una hipótesis comprobable. T3 introduce niveles y campos de logging seguros. T4 decide cuándo abortar, cuándo cuarentenar y cuándo un retry puede ser seguro.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Criterio de cierre inicio CP-N1-C...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Criterio de cierre: CP-N1-C, el tercer incremento del proyecto acumulativo del Nivel 1, produce una bitácora auditable que distingue fallos de datos, configuración y proveedor, propaga un correlation_id y evita que tanto el mensaje del log como la excepción adjunta revelen correo, teléfono o dirección completos.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Reutiliza normalizadores S05-S07 y conteos reconciliados S08... S10 CLI...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: S09 reutiliza datos sintéticos y algunos artefactos de S05-S08, pero no presume que sus modelos incompletos de provenance, exit status o exceptions ya estén dominados. S10 empaquetará este contrato en una CLI y hará explícita la traducción entre excepciones fatales y códigos de salida del proceso.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: CASO-LIM-009... C00x... @ejemplo.pe...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: CASO-LIM-009 es el incidente sintético utilizado en S09: registros ficticios C00x, correos del dominio de ejemplo y montos de laboratorio. Nunca uses datos personales reales ni interpretes estos logs como evidencia de fraude o parentesco.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Prefiere tipos concretos... except Exception amplio...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Captura el tipo más específico que corresponda a la operación que realmente puedes manejar. ValueError indica un valor incompatible con el contrato de una operación; TypeError, un tipo de objeto inadecuado; KeyError, una clave ausente; FileNotFoundError, un archivo que no se encontró. except Exception puede ser razonable en la frontera del proceso para registrar un fallo inesperado, siempre que preserves la excepción original y no la tragues.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: raise ValueError... Decimal... raise NewError from e...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: raise detiene la ruta normal y crea o propaga una excepción. Añade contexto seguro, como record_id y reason_code, pero no insertes valores personales o secretos que luego puedan aparecer en un traceback. Para montos, declara primero el formato aceptado y crea Decimal desde ese texto; no conviertas separadores ambiguos por sustitución global. raise NuevaExcepcion(...) from e conserva explícitamente la causa original.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: excepción personalizada ligera class DataLoadError(Exception)...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Primero practica esta política con excepciones incorporadas. Si el curso conserva una excepción personalizada aquí, introduce solo el mínimo imprescindible: class DataLoadError(Exception): pass crea un nuevo tipo de excepción que pertenece a la familia Exception. No intentes enseñar todavía el modelo general de clases; S11 lo hará. Mantén mensajes libres de raw sensible.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: try/except/else/finally... with hace lo mismo vía context managers...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: En un try, except maneja únicamente las excepciones que declares; else corre si el try terminó sin excepción; finally corre al salir del bloque tanto en éxito como durante propagación y se usa sobre todo para cleanup. Un with usa un context manager: un objeto que ejecuta acciones de entrada y salida alrededor del bloque. Para archivos y StringIO, esa salida cierra el recurso incluso cuando el cuerpo falla.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: No uses except bare... manejar vs propagar...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: No uses except: ni except Exception: pass como forma de recuperación. Captura solo un fallo para el que esta capa tenga una acción definida: cuarentenar la unidad, traducir la excepción conservando la causa o registrar y relanzar. Si la capa no puede recuperar el contrato, deja que la excepción siga hacia una frontera superior.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Config rota fail-fast; fila inválida cuarentena...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Una configuración imprescindible rota hace fallar el job: no basta imprimir 'fatal'. Una fila inválida puede ir a cuarentena y permitir que el lote continúe cuando la política de esa fuente lo autoriza. Reconciliar conteos es obligatorio pero no suficiente: también deben cumplirse los límites de cuarentena y la presencia de inputs críticos.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: traceback lista frames del más reciente al más profundo (o viceversa)...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: En el traceback estándar de Python, lee primero la última línea para conocer clase y mensaje; luego mira el último frame de tu código, que suele ser la operación inmediata que falló. Los frames anteriores muestran los callers que llevaron hasta allí. No asumas que un frame de biblioteca es la causa: sube o baja en la cadena según la evidencia, pero conserva siempre el orden concreto que muestra la herramienta.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: breakpoint/pdb... traceback.format_exc + prints controlados...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un traceback es evidencia estática; un debugger permite detener la ejecución y observar estado en ese punto. En una sesión local puedes llamar breakpoint(), inspeccionar una variable segura y continuar. traceback.format_exc() sirve para obtener el texto de la excepción dentro de un except, pero también incluye su mensaje: no lo imprimas ni lo registres si ese mensaje puede contener datos sensibles.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: nunca imprimas secretos ni PII completos en variables locales...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: No captures ni vuelques locals indiscriminadamente. Los tracebacks normales no muestran todos los valores locales, pero sí muestran el texto de la excepción, y herramientas de debugging pueden exponer más estado. Diseña excepciones con reason codes y referencias seguras; conserva evidencia sensible en un canal separado y protegido. El enmascarado reduce exposición, no elimina la necesidad de controles de acceso.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Minimal repro: menor entrada que dispara el bug... SoloNombre...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un minimal repro es el conjunto más pequeño de código, datos y condiciones que todavía produce el comportamiento. A veces eso significa una sola cadena como SoloNombre; otras veces necesitas conservar configuración o estado. El objetivo no es ganar por longitud, sino eliminar todo lo que no participa causalmente en el fallo.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: hipótesis falsables... 3 tokens truncado...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Escribe una predicción que pueda fallar antes de editar el código. Ejemplo: 'si el bug se debe a asumir al menos dos tokens, SoloNombre debe fallar y Ana Perez debe pasar; el caso Maria Lopez Garcia revela además un segundo bug silencioso de truncamiento'. Ejecuta ambos casos y registra cuál hipótesis sobrevivió.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: test de regresión rojo→verde... 5-whys...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Convierte el minimal repro en una comprobación que falle antes del arreglo. Aplica el cambio mínimo, ejecuta la misma comprobación hasta verla pasar y vuelve a ejecutar un caso vecino que antes era correcto. Ese rojo→verde demuestra la reparación cubierta por el test; no demuestra que todos los nombres posibles estén resueltos. Usa los porqués para investigar por qué el contrato permitió el caso, no para renombrar el síntoma como causa raíz.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: DEBUG INFO WARNING ERROR CRITICAL...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Usa DEBUG para detalle diagnóstico, INFO para eventos normales del job, WARNING para una condición inesperada de la que el programa puede continuar, ERROR cuando una operación no pudo completarse y CRITICAL cuando el proceso o servicio puede no poder continuar. La severidad exacta de una cuarentena depende de la política operativa: no conviertas cada fila esperablemente inválida en una alerta ERROR.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Logger de módulo... handlers/formatters entrypoint... log.exception...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: logging es un módulo incluido con Python. Un logger de módulo, obtenido con logging.getLogger(__name__), emite eventos sin configurar por sí mismo todos sus destinos; la aplicación configura handlers y formatters en su frontera. Dentro de un except, log.exception añade traceback y mensaje de la excepción: úsalo solo cuando esa excepción ya sea segura para el destino del log.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Logs estructurados (key=value o JSON) con campos estables...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Distingue texto semi-estructurado de campos reales. stage=normalize dentro del mensaje solo es un campo si existe un parser acordado. Con stdlib puedes añadir atributos al LogRecord mediante extra={...} y hacer que el Formatter los emita de forma estable. Esa estructura permite filtrar sin depender del orden o la redacción del mensaje humano.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: CASO-LIM-009... stage/record_id... triage minutos...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: En CASO-LIM-009, el incidente sintético, cada evento lleva stage y un correlation_id de la corrida. Incluye record_id solo si la política de logging permite ese identificador y no necesitas un token menos identificable. Estos campos ayudan a unir eventos, pero no vuelven inocuo al log: sigue aplicando minimización, controles de acceso y retención.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: correlation_id viaja CLI → service → repo... manifest S08...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un correlation_id se crea una vez al comenzar una corrida y se pasa explícitamente a cada operación que deba registrar eventos de esa misma corrida. En S09 basta demostrar dos capas sencillas —por ejemplo procesar_lote(correlation_id) llama validar_fila(correlation_id)—. La arquitectura CLI/service/repo se estudiará cuando esos conceptos sean formales.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Nunca loguees email/teléfono/dirección completos... máscaras estables...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: No registres email, teléfono o dirección completos en el canal operativo. Si un caso necesita una referencia humana, aplica una máscara aprobada y conserva solo el mínimo necesario. La máscara reduce exposición pero puede seguir siendo identificable cuando se combina con record_id, dominio, tiempo u otros campos; por eso el log sigue sujeto a acceso y retención controlados.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: helpers mask... único camino... log.exception stack + correlation_id sin PII...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Centraliza las transformaciones de logging seguro, pero recuerda que no solo el mensaje explícito llega al log. log.exception también adjunta la excepción y su texto. Por eso las excepciones que puedan registrarse deben contener únicamente reason codes, IDs seguros y contexto no sensible. Demuestra email, teléfono y dirección; después registra el evento con el mismo correlation_id que recibió la capa.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: data/config/provider: timeout S3, HTTP 503...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Clasifica primero por política que esta capa entiende. data: un valor de entrada incumple el contrato; config: una opción necesaria para toda la corrida falta o es inválida; external/transient: una operación externa puede intentarse de nuevo según el contrato del proveedor. En S09 usa TimeoutError simulado como ejemplo; HTTP 503 y servicios como Amazon S3 se estudiarán cuando exista un modelo de HTTP/API.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Fail-fast config; quarantine data; reconcile in==ok+quarantined...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Una configuración crítica inválida debe terminar la corrida con estado de fallo; registrar 'abort' y continuar hasta exit 0 no cumple fail-fast. Una fila de datos inválida puede ir a cuarentena si la política permite continuar. La reconciliación confirma que sabes dónde quedó cada unidad, pero el gate de éxito debe revisar además las condiciones de calidad y fuentes críticas.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Éxito parcial válido si manifest cuadra... fail closed...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un lote reconciliado puede ser candidato a éxito parcial, no éxito automático. Antes de publicar comprueba también las reglas de aceptación: fuentes requeridas presentes, categorías de error permitidas y umbral máximo de cuarentena cuando exista. Fail closed significa que cualquier condición crítica incumplida bloquea la publicación y deja un estado de fallo observable por el proceso que invocó el job.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Retry solo errores transitorios TimeoutError, HTTP503, red... ValueError no...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Reintenta únicamente fallos que el contrato de la operación clasifique como transitorios y solo cuando repetir la operación sea seguro. Un TimeoutError puede significar que no recibiste respuesta, no necesariamente que el servidor no actuó. Un error de validación de datos no mejora por repetirlo: se maneja según la política de datos, normalmente cuarentena.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: Operaciones idempotentes (misma clave de escritura) permiten volver a ejecutar...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Una operación es idempotente cuando repetir la misma solicitud lógica deja el mismo resultado observable que ejecutarla una sola vez. Una idempotency key puede ayudar solo si el receptor la hace cumplir: por ejemplo, detecta una clave ya procesada y devuelve el resultado anterior o hace un upsert en vez de un segundo INSERT. Elegir una tupla como clave sin enforcement no evita duplicados.

paragraph_audit.current_content_excerpt: backoff creciente... jitter... max_attempts... nunca retries infinitos...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Entre intentos, aumenta la espera para reducir presión sobre el servicio. En sistemas con muchos workers se añade jitter, una variación aleatoria limitada, para evitar reintentos sincronizados. max_attempts debe ser finito. Al agotarlo, aplica la política de esa operación: cuarentena solo si tiene sentido para esa unidad; de lo contrario falla el job. Ningún backoff vuelve segura una operación no idempotente.

artifact_audit.improved_strategy: Use built-in ValueError/RuntimeError for first chaining trace, declare accepted amount syntax, keep exception messages PII-safe.
Move boundary to publication/job decision and show row-level recovery remains available through validation.

artifact_audit.execution_check: standalone process returned 0 after printing fatal
artifact_audit.improved_strategy: Let fatal exception escape or re-raise at process boundary; show handle.closed rather than printing a hard-coded cleanup claim.

issues: catching Exception does not erase concrete type
boundary catch does not inherently lose origin context

artifact_audit.improved_strategy: Show one short full traceback annotated in order, then a separate breakpoint walkthrough.
Manual minimal case plus one failing assertion, fix, passing assertion and neighbor case.

issues: fields are message text rather than LogRecord fields
artifact_audit.improved_strategy: Use extra fields and a Formatter; either measure duration or label fixed value as fixture.

artifact_audit.execution_check: masked explicit message still leaked a full email from exception text in traceback
artifact_audit.improved_strategy: PII-safe exception messages + explicit correlation propagation + all promised masks.

issues: fatal config error caught then normal exit 0
artifact_audit.execution_check: standalone process returned 0 after printing abort
artifact_audit.improved_strategy: Separate library raise from process-boundary policy; do not label swallowed exception fail-fast.
First retry a side-effect-free read; then demonstrate enforced idempotency in a tiny fake store; use named functions for error cases.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: finally does not run during an unhandled exception
rejected_findings.reason: Python executes finally before the exception continues propagating in normal interpreter control flow.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: raise NewError(...) from e loses the original cause
rejected_findings.reason: Explicit exception chaining preserves the direct cause and the interpreter/traceback module can display both.
Catching alone does not erase the concrete type/traceback; swallowing or replacing without preservation is the actual problem.
Module-level loggers are standard guidance; configuration placement is the real concern.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: log.exception should be used outside except
rejected_findings.reason: The lesson uses it inside an exception handler; the confirmed issue is sensitive exception text, not call placement.
Retries are appropriate for some transient operations when retryability and idempotency/known outcome are established.
Masking materially reduces exposure; the defect is claiming it guarantees non-identification or automatically makes logs shareable.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: custom exceptions are technically invalid before OOP
rejected_findings.reason: The code is valid Python. The confirmed defect is pedagogical placement: class/inheritance syntax precedes its canonical teaching point.

concept_ledger_delta.reason: Basic effect is shown, but custom-class and privacy-heavy examples obscure the first model.
Core clauses are described correctly, but process-boundary and with examples create false fail-fast evidence.
from e is demonstrated, but nested cause trace is not fully read and custom classes add future syntax.
Conflicting direction rules and false boundary figure.
Useful idea but narrowed to shortest failing input.
Definitions and severity progression are sufficiently clear after minor policy caveat.
Canonical code embeds key=value in a free-form message.
Traceback inclusion can bypass masking through exception text.
Purpose is clear but propagation is not demonstrated.
Masking is overstated as non-identification and exception text bypasses helpers.
Fatal demo paths catch errors and exit 0.
Data/config distinction is useful but reconciliation is treated as sufficient for partial success.
Same key is presented as if it creates idempotent behavior without enforcement.
Retryability is overgeneralized and executable example lacks side-effect/idempotency evidence.
Imports continue to be used without the S10 mental model.
S09 repeats caught-fatal/exit-0 behavior from S08.

P1: Replace conflicting traceback directions with one annotated standard traceback.
Remove or microdefine custom exception classes before S11.
Make fatal examples produce a real failing process state or re-raise; never label caught exit-0 examples fail-fast.
Redesign exception/logging privacy so log.exception cannot reintroduce raw PII through exception messages.
Actually teach debugger use and a red-green regression cycle.
Use actual LogRecord fields or stop calling key=value message text structured fields.
Demonstrate correlation propagation and all promised masks.
Repair idempotency and retry mental models with enforceable side-effect examples.
P2: Downgrade exception type from diagnosis to clue/classification evidence.
Reject ambiguous monetary separators rather than replacing commas globally.
Microdefine with/context managers and stdlib imports.
Define minimal repro beyond shortest input and remove generator-expression distraction.
State masking is reduction, not anonymization.
Replace S3/HTTP/provider jargon with bounded current-level examples.

next_round_watchlist: S10 is the canonical module/import/packaging/CLI section. Imports used throughout S01-S09 remain MENTION_ONLY and must be taught from first principles.

S10 must explicitly repair process exit semantics: S08 and S09 both printed fatal/abort while returning actual exit status 0. Library exceptions, CLI catches, stderr and sys.exit/return codes must be separated.
if __name__ == '__main__' appeared in S01 but remains MENTION_ONLY; S10 cannot say 'as you already know'.
Traceback, fail-fast and log.exception remain MISCONCEPTION_RISK from S09; CLI error handlers must not build on them silently.
Logging levels are USABLE, but structured fields/correlation propagation/privacy are not.
Custom classes remain MENTION_ONLY until S11; S10 should avoid custom OO abstractions as scaffolding for modules.
JSON/provenance remain partial from S08 and should not be prerequisites for CLI configuration examples without local bridges.
Idempotency/retry remain unsafe and should not be presumed by any S10 command retry behavior.
CP-N1-C/CASO identifiers remain a persistent widow-term family unless expanded globally.
